Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake target policy. I’ll first follow the workspace contract in `README.md`, then the skill’s visual-evidence procedure, and only then inspect or edit the candidate and guidance files.

The assigned guidance already identifies `oscillator_energy_gain=2.1` as the current compact-route anchor, while warning that several small guard, gain, and damping tweaks caused nonlinear route regressions. I’m now checking that distilled account directly against every sampled rollout, including the weakest finite run because this sample contains no outright failure.

The skill-guided visual comparison shows a reproducible distinction: all three `2.1` sheets are identical and take the compact wake route, while the isolated `2.2` gain takes a deeper lower arc and corrects later. Diagnostics confirm that `2.2` lowers peak joint angle/speed slightly but worsens arrival, mean distance, upstream-relative propulsion, effort, and loads. I’ll record the resulting split-gain hypothesis before touching the policy, as required.

The durable guidance now records the concrete `2.2` negative result: lower joint peaks did not translate into lower aggregate load or a better route, so future work should not extrapolate the uniform gain above `2.1`. The new candidate instead isolates the untested above-orbit damping branch and leaves every established gait/steering/guard value unchanged.

The mandated guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace inconsistency before evaluating my lesson: `README.md` contains the same assigned parent entry twice, so the checker sees two “copied to guidance” markers and stops. I’m inspecting the local checker and parent copies to determine whether this can be repaired without changing any out-of-scope file.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicated parent marker from the rendered README. The policy contract command itself cannot start because this workspace image has no `julia` on `PATH`; I’m checking the local toolchain locations before treating that as an environment-only limitation.

I’ve completed the local checks: guidance update PASS, boundary PASS, candidate non-empty, and every `params.FIELD` reference maps to a returned parameter. Per the workspace instruction, I’m now invoking the configured check-runner for an independent final audit; its Julia step may report the same missing-runtime limitation.
